Fairness of a lineup from mock witnesses

Source: R/lnroc.R
lnsize.Rd

Asks whether a lineup singles out its suspect. People who never saw the crime (mock witnesses) read the witness's description and pick the lineup member who fits it best; in a fair lineup of k they pick each member about equally often. From their choices:

Usage

lnsize(choice, k = NULL, susp = 1, level = 0.95)

Arguments

choice

The lineup position each mock witness picked: whole numbers from 1.

k

NULL for the largest position picked, or the lineup's size: one whole number from 2.

susp

The suspect's position: one whole number from 1 to k.

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class lnsize, a list: count, the choices of each position; stat, a named vector (n, k, psusp, pbin, fsize, esize, etr, etrlo, etrhi); and susp.

Details

  • psusp, the share who picked the suspect, and pbin, the binomial chance of that many or more if each member were picked with chance 1 / k (a small pbin is bias against the suspect);

  • fsize, the functional size, the number of mock witnesses over those who picked the suspect (Wells, Leippe and Ostrom 1979; k for a fair lineup);

  • esize, Malpass's (1981) effective size, k - sum |o_i - e| / (2 e) with o_i the choices of member i and e = n / k: how many members are plausible;

  • etr, Tredoux's (1998) effective size 1 / sum p_i^2, p_i the share choosing member i, with a delta-method interval from the multinomial variance of sum p_i^2, 4 (sum p^3 - (sum p^2)^2) / n.

References

Malpass, R. S. (1981). Effective size and defendant bias in eyewitness identification lineups. Law and Human Behavior, 5(4), 299-309. doi:10.1007/BF01044945

Tredoux, C. G. (1998). Statistical inference on measures of lineup fairness. Law and Human Behavior, 22(2), 217-237. doi:10.1023/A:1025746220886

Wells, G. L., Leippe, M. R. and Ostrom, T. M. (1979). Guidelines for empirically assessing the fairness of a lineup. Law and Human Behavior, 3(4), 285-293. doi:10.1007/BF01039807

Examples

# 40 mock witnesses, a lineup of six, the suspect in position 3
ch <- c(rep(3, 15), rep(1, 5), rep(2, 6), rep(4, 4), rep(5, 7), rep(6, 3))
lnsize(ch, k = 6, susp = 3)
#> lnsize: 40 mock witnesses, lineup of 6, suspect in position 3
#>            n            k        psusp         pbin        fsize        esize 
#> 40.000000000  6.000000000  0.375000000  0.001282306  2.666666667  4.700000000 
#>          etr        etrlo        etrhi 
#>  4.444444444  2.984575856  5.904313032
